text:
Folks, I hate, hate, hate to agree with JD Vance, a man who has probably sold his soul more times than he has changed his name. However, he was correct when he said this about Israel in an interview with The NYT: “You're a country of nine million people. You can't just kill your way out of solving every single national security problem that you have.”

Then again, he also said, “[Iran’s] nuclear weapons program is destroyed. It is gone."

Yeah, so let’s not go and give him too much credit.

Regardless, we’re witnessing a massive fissure that I never imagined I’d see during my lifetime. Israel, through its belligerent, genocidal leadership, has broken its bipartisan hold on American politics. To preserve his rule, Netanyahu and Israel supporters went all-in with Donald Trump.

What they failed to realize is that Trump is only loyal to himself in the end.

After a disastrous four months where the U.S. clearly lost the illegal Iran War, Trump seems to be done and wants a clean break. The 14-point MOU between both countries represents a massive win for Iran, which has emerged stronger and more influential in the region. Had Trump simply stayed in the Obama deal, none of this would have happened, but of course he was the first President in 47 years to be dogwalked by Netanyahu into this ongoing quagmire.

Now, Trump’s poll numbers are rock bottom, the economy is worse, the cost of living has increased, and Israel has emerged as a global pariah due to its ongoing genocide and its current occupation of Southern Lebanon.

Israel has already signaled it will not abide by these terms. As history has proven time and time again, Israel will use any unethical, illegal, and murderous means possible to ensure it can sabotage this deal and bully its supporters. It has already activated its right-wing minions in America to loudly criticize the deal. This includes Christian Zionists, such as Mike Huckabee, who is the US Ambassador to Israel, war hawks, and Israel-first MAGA pundits.

A lot can and will happen over the next few weeks. The United States, Israel, and the Middle East are on the precipice of massive changes in terms of global relationships, power dynamics, and influence that will shape the world for at least a decade.  I invited Palestinian journalist and author Rula Jebreal to break it all down.
